what is the differences between here and reddit?

The most obvious difference (to a new user) is that upvotes/downvotes are limited. You can only give out a certain number of upvotes per day until you reach 20 CCP (that would be comment karma on reddit), and you can't downvote at all until you reach 100 CCP.

Another big difference is transparency. "Modlogs" are visible to the public. For example, you can see every submission that the /v/askvoat mods have deleted here.
People will answer this question instead of it just disappearing into the ether.

So far there is less of an "echo chamber" vibe here. This leads to livelier discussions and a wider array of content. It will be interesting to see if this lasts if there is another influx of users in a couple of days.

The difference is the people who make reddit what it is haven't moved over. The downvote brigades, the moronic pun chains, the people who just comment in memes... they're all still on reddit. For now.

Give it time, those types will eventually make their way over here.

Luckily there are core differences here that should help keep it somewhat controlled... hopefully if we build a strong enough community now, when those types come over they'll get discouraged with the wait on downvoating and limited upvoats.
